mainTopic: Two חטאות for entering and withdrawing from a woman who becomes a נדה, and whether limp relations with עריות bring liability.
overview: רבא looks for a case where a man brings two חטאות when a woman becomes a נדה during relations: one for entering and one for withdrawing. The near-the-וסת case does not work for an עם הארץ, and the not-near-the-וסת case does not work for anyone. So רבא settles on a man who knows one הלכה but not the other. רבא shows that both liabilities are taught in משניות: withdrawal in our משנה, and entry in the משנה in נדה about blood found on his cloth. רב אדא בר מתנא reads that נדה משנה as a withdrawal case instead. רבינא challenges him from the word 'found', and רבא backs רבינא. רב אדא brings a ברייתא calling it a מצות עשה, and רבא answers that words are missing from it. The גמרא then asks how the man should withdraw: he should stay still until he is limp. רבא learns from this that limp relations with עריות are exempt. אביי disagrees, and רבה בר חנן challenges אביי's view.

steps.title: An ignorant man would bring only one חטאת
steps.stepSummary: If the man is an עם הארץ, his entry and withdrawal both happen during one lapse of awareness, so he brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is an ignorant person, then this and that are like eating two olive-sizes of forbidden fat in one lapse of awareness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still testing the case where relations happened near her וסת. Here it knocks out the possibility that the man is an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ does not know either prohibition. So nothing reminds him that he sinned between entering and withdrawing. Two sins under one העלם bring only one חטאת, like eating two כזיתים of חלב in one lapse of awareness.

keyTerms.meaning: An unlearned person who does not know the הלכות involved

phrases.english: And if it is with an ignorant person,
this and that (entry and withdrawal)

phrases.aramaic: ״אָכַל שְׁנֵי זֵיתֵי חֵלֶב בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד״ הוּא!
phrases.english: is like 'he ate two olive-sizes of forbidden fat in one lapse of awareness'!
phrases.notes: That case brings only one חטאת, since he never realized his mistake in between the two acts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier testing of the near-the-וסת case. The תלמיד חכם option was already dealt with before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that the near-the-וסת case is about an עם הארץ
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is a single העלם across both acts, so he brings only one חטאת, not two.

steps.title: Trying the case where it was not near her וסת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a case where relations were not near her expected period, and asks which kind of man is involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps it is when relations were not near her expected period? And with whom?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the near-the-וסת case failed, the גמרא tries the other case. It sets up the next move by asking what kind of man we are talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not near her וסת, the man had no reason to expect bleeding. Before the גמרא can test this case, it has to decide whether the man is learned or ignorant.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to her expected time of menstruation
And with whom (which kind of person)?

phrases.english: Rather, when it is not near her expected period?
And with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the near-the-וסת case fails, this offers the other case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the not-near-the-וסת case can give two חטאות, and which kind of man that would be.

steps.title: The not-near-the-וסת case fails for both kinds of men
steps.stepSummary: For a תלמיד חכם there is no חטאת at all: the entry was אונס and the withdrawal was מזיד. For an עם הארץ there is only one חטאת, for the withdrawal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a Torah scholar, he is not liable even one: for the entry he was forced by circumstances, and for the withdrawal he acted on purpose! If an ignorant person, he is liable only one, for the withdrawal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests both kinds of men in the not-near-the-וסת case. Neither one gives two חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not near her וסת, the entry was completely blameless (אונס), so the entry can never bring a חטאת. A scholar who withdraws immediately knows it is forbidden, so his act is מזיד, and a חטאת is only for שוגג. An עם הארץ withdraws by mistake, so he gets only one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar who knows the הלכות
Forced by circumstances, not at fault

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the scholar gets off free here. His withdrawal is on purpose, and a חטאת is only for mistaken sins, so it simply does not apply to him.

phrases.english: If you say with a Torah scholar,
he is not liable even one (sin-offering);
for the entry he was forced by circumstances,
for the withdrawal he acted on purpose!
If with an ignorant person,
he is liable only one, for the withdrawal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by testing both kinds of men and rejecting both.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The entry is אונס, so it never brings a חטאת. That leaves at most one חטאת.

steps.title: רבא: a scholar for one rule but not the other
steps.stepSummary: רבא goes back to the near-the-וסת case. The man knows one הלכה but not the other, so he has two separate lapses of awareness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: Actually it is near her expected period, and with a Torah scholar, but a scholar for this הלכה and not a scholar for that one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reconsiders and gives a new answer. He uses the near-the-וסת case with a man who is only partly learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man knows it is forbidden to be with her near her וסת. He wrongly thought he would finish in time, so his entry is שוגג. Once she says she became impure, he realizes that sin, so the first העלם ends. But he does not know that immediate withdrawal is forbidden, so the withdrawal is a new שוגג under a new העלם. That makes two חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and said (he reconsidered)

steps.whatToRemember: Two חטאות need two separate lapses of awareness. A man who knows one הלכה but not the other has exactly that.

phrases.english: Rava went back and said:
Actually, it is near her expected period,
and with a Torah scholar,
and he is a scholar for this (הלכה)
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule against relations near her וסת.

phrases.english: but not a scholar for that one.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the rule against withdrawing immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם בְּסָמוּךְ לְוִסְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both cases failed, רבא returns to the near-the-וסת case with a new kind of man.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the man as partly learned
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man is either fully learned or fully ignorant, so the case does not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: He knows one הלכה but not the other, which creates two separate lapses of awareness and two חטאות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that liability is counted by lapses of awareness, not just by the number of acts.

steps.title: Both liabilities are taught in משניות, starting with withdrawal
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both liabilities, entry and withdrawal, are already taught in משניות. He first shows that our משנה teaches withdrawal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We learned both of them; we learned entry, and we learned withdrawal. Withdrawal we learned, as it teaches: If he was with a pure woman and she told him 'I became impure,' and he withdrew immediately, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says both liabilities are already taught in משניות. He begins with our משנה, which is the source for withdrawal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a man who withdraws immediately after she says 'I became impure' is חייב. That shows the withdrawal itself is a forbidden act that can bring a חטאת. The next step brings the proof for entry.

phrases.english: Rava said: And we learned both of them;
we learned entry, we learned withdrawal.
Withdrawal we learned, as it teaches:
If he was having relations with a pure woman
and she said to him, 'I have become impure,'
and he withdrew immediately, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the two liabilities from step 4 with the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: 'He was having relations with a pure woman... and he withdrew immediately, he is liable.'

steps.title: רבא shows where the משנה teaches liability for entry
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the משנה in נדה: if blood is found on his cloth, both are impure and must bring a קרבן. He reads it as a case near her expected period, so the liability is for the entry.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have also learned about entry: 'If blood is found on his cloth, they are impure and must bring a קרבן.' Isn't this a case near her expected period, and the liability is for the entry?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes the proof he started in step 5. He already showed where the משנה teaches withdrawal, and now he shows where it teaches entry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on the man's cloth shows the bleeding started during relations. רבא assumes this happened near her expected period. In that case the man should have been careful from the start, so his entry itself counts as a שגגה that needs a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: On his cloth, the one he wipes with after relations
Near the time her period is expected

phrases.english: Entry, we have learned it:
phrases.notes: This quote is from the משנה in נדה 14a.

phrases.english: If [blood] is found on his [cloth],
they are impure and liable to bring an offering.
What, is it not near her expected period,
and [the liability is] for the entry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 5 by adding the source for entry.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can be liable for entry when relations were near her expected period
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה נדה: 'found on his cloth, they are impure and liable to a קרבן'

steps.title: רב אדא says the משנה may be about withdrawal
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא says the משנה can be read as a case not near her expected period, where the liability is for withdrawing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנא said to רבא: Really, I can tell you it is a case not near her expected period, and the liability is for the withdrawal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא pushes back on רבא's proof. He offers another way to read the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is not near her period, the entry was innocent. The only sin is pulling out the wrong way after he learned she was bleeding. So the משנה would not prove anything about entry.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (a phrase that offers another reading)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said to Rava:
Actually, I can say to you,
[it is] where it was not near her expected period,
and [he is liable] for the withdrawal;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's reading of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof for entry, not the הלכה itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can also be explained as a case not near her period, with liability for withdrawal.

steps.title: Why the משנה would repeat the case of withdrawal
steps.stepSummary: Someone might ask why the משנה in נדה would teach withdrawal again. רב אדא answers that the real lesson is the case of 'found on her cloth', and 'his cloth' is mentioned only alongside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: why teach withdrawal again, since it was already taught? The answer is that we needed the lesson of 'found on her cloth': they are impure because of a doubt but do not bring a קרבן. Since the משנה needed to teach 'her cloth', it also taught 'his cloth'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא answers a challenge to his own reading before anyone raises it. He explains why the משנה would repeat a law we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is that withdrawal was already taught in our משנה. The answer is that the new lesson is in 'her cloth'. There it is a doubt whether the bleeding started during relations, so there is no קרבן. The 'his cloth' line was added only to go along with that case, which is what the גמרא means by אַיְּידֵי.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (opens an expected objection)
Since, along the way (it was taught only because of the other case)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two cloths apart. 'שלו' (his cloth) shows the bleeding happened during relations, so there is a קרבן. 'שלה' (her cloth) might mean it began only afterward, so there is no קרבן.

phrases.english: And if you would say: why do I need [to learn about] withdrawal,
since he already taught it?
phrases.notes: He means the תנא already taught withdrawal in our משנה here in שבועות.

phrases.english: This was needed to teach us:
If [blood] is found on her [cloth],
they are impure because of doubt, and exempt from an offering;

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְּידֵי דְּבָעֵי מִיתְנֵא נִמְצָא עַל שֶׁלָּהּ,
phrases.english: and since it needed to teach 'found on her [cloth]',
it also taught 'found on his [cloth]'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב אדא's reading from an expected challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The case was taught along the way (אגב)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'his cloth' case would just repeat what we already know about withdrawal
steps.terutzMaskana: It is written only to go with the new lesson of 'her cloth'

steps.title: רבינא: 'found' means he learned only afterward
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אדא. The word 'found' means the blood was discovered after relations. In a withdrawal case, he already knew when he withdrew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אדא: Can you really explain that משנה as not near her period, with liability for withdrawal? It says 'found', which means afterward. If it were about withdrawal, he knew from the start, when he withdrew!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אדא's reading by looking closely at one word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Withdrawal liability means he was told during relations and pulled out the wrong way, so he knew right then. Finding blood on the cloth later adds nothing to that. So the משנה's 'found' fits only a case where he discovered it afterward, which means the liability is for the entry.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really explain it as (a challenge to a proposed reading)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Adda:
Can you really establish that [משנה]
as not near her expected period, and for the withdrawal?!
But it teaches 'is found',
and 'is found' implies afterward;
and if it is for withdrawal,
from the start, when he withdrew,
from the start he had knowledge!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אדא's reading from steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא's reading of the משנה as a withdrawal case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Found' means he discovered it later. In withdrawal he already knew during the act, so the discovery would add nothing.

steps.title: רבא tells Rav Adda to accept רבינא's point
steps.stepSummary: רבא backs רבינא and tells רב אדא to listen to what his teacher is saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Listen to what your teacher is saying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sides with רבינא's objection and presses רב אדא to give up his reading. This sets up רב אדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. רבא is adding weight to רבינא's challenge, which supports רבא's own original proof for entry.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Listen to what your teacher is saying.

steps.title: רב אדא: a ברייתא calls this case a positive מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא answers that a ברייתא on this משנה calls it the מצות עשה of נדה. Entry would be a לא תעשה, so the case must be about withdrawal.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can I listen? A ברייתא taught on it: 'This is the positive מצוה of נדה for which one is liable.' If it were about entry, that would be a prohibition, not a positive מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא defends his reading by bringing a ברייתא that comments on the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being with a נדה is a לא תעשה. The ברייתא calls this case a מצות עשה, which only fits the withdrawal, meaning how he must pull away. So the ברייתא supports reading the משנה as a withdrawal case.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches about it

steps.whatToRemember: רבא reads the משנה ('found on his cloth') as entry near her period. רב אדא reads it as withdrawal. רבינא's argument from 'found' supports רבא. The ברייתא's 'מצות עשה' seems to support רב אדא, but רבא answers this in the next step by restoring missing words.

phrases.english: How can I listen?
phrases.notes: The speaker here is רב אדא answering רבא.

phrases.english: For it was taught about it:
This is the positive mitzvah regarding a נדה
for which one is liable,
and if it is so [that it is about entry],
it is a prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אדא defends his reading against רבינא and רבא.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה in נדה is about withdrawal
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'This is the מצות עשה of נדה for which one is liable'

steps.title: רבא restores missing words in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב אדא that the ברייתא is missing words. Once corrected, it has two cases: a לא תעשה case and a separate מצות עשה case about withdrawing right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you learned it that way, words are missing. Teach it like this: 'This is the לא תעשה of נדה for which one is liable.' And: 'If he was with a pure woman and she said I became impure, and he withdrew immediately, he is liable. This is the מצות עשה of נדה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב אדא's proof from the ברייתא by saying the ברייתא is missing some words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא argued that because the ברייתא calls the case a מצות עשה, the משנה must be about withdrawing. רבא answers that the label 'לא תעשה' really belongs to the 'found on his cloth' case, and the 'מצות עשה' label belongs to a separate, missing case of withdrawing right away. So רב אדא's proof is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing; teach it like this

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying the same case is both a לא תעשה and a מצות עשה. Once the missing words are put back, these are two different cases with two different labels.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבא answering רב אדא.

phrases.english: If you learned it that way, words are missing, and teach it like this:
This is the prohibition
regarding a נדה for which one is liable.
If he was having relations with a pure woman
and she said to him, 'I have become impure,'
and he withdrew immediately, he is liable;

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁבְּנִדָּה כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: this is the positive command regarding a נדה, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אדא's proof from the ברייתא in step 11 by restoring missing words.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the משנה's case must be about withdrawing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא as רב אדא learned it is missing words. The 'מצות עשה' label belongs to a separate withdrawal case, not to the 'found on his cloth' case.

steps.title: How should he withdraw?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ruling that withdrawing immediately makes him liable and asks what the man should actually do.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If he withdrew immediately, he is liable. So what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ruling about withdrawing right away and sets up a practical question: what is the right way to act?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If staying is forbidden and pulling out right away also brings liability, the man seems stuck. The גמרא asks for the correct behavior, and the answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: The Master said:
If he withdrew immediately, he is liable.
What should he do?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: פֵּירַשׁ מִיָּד – חַיָּיב. הֵיכִי עָבֵיד?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the withdrawal ruling of our משנה (quoted in step 5 and again in step 12) and asks how to carry it out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The proper way for the man to withdraw so that he is not liable.

steps.title: Wait without moving until no longer aroused
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, quoting רבא, says the man should press his fingernails into the ground and stay still until he is limp, and only then withdraw.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רבא: He presses his ten fingernails into the ground until it becomes limp, and that is good for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the answer: the man should hold himself completely still until he is no longer aroused, and only then pull out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since withdrawing right away makes him liable, the proper way is to stay still and withdraw only once he is no longer aroused. Why waiting helps is argued in the coming steps: רבא says limp contact is not a liable act, and אביי says the waiting man is exempt as אנוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Until it 'dies', meaning until he is no longer aroused
And that is good for him

phrases.english: רב הונא said in the name of רבא:
He presses his ten fingernails into the ground
phrases.notes: 'Ground' here means the bed he is lying on. He grips it to keep himself still.

phrases.english: until it becomes limp, and that is good for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: נוֹעֵץ עֶשֶׂר צִפׇּרְנָיו בַּקַּרְקַע
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He should stay still until he is no longer aroused, and then withdraw.

steps.title: רבא: relations in a limp state with עריות is exempt
steps.stepSummary: From רב הונא's ruling, רבא concludes that relations with עריות in a limp state carry no liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches that one who has relations in a limp state with forbidden relatives is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws a new rule from the instruction to wait. The reasoning behind it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Withdrawing in a limp state is still a kind of physical contact. רבא learns from the exemption here that contact in a limp state with עריות is not a punishable act at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This teaches', a formula for drawing a rule from a ruling
One who has relations in a limp state

phrases.english: רבא said: This teaches
that one who has relations in a limp state with forbidden relatives is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule about עריות from רב הונא's practical instruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations in a limp state with עריות carry no liability.

steps.title: Why the exemption cannot be because he is אנוס
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his rule: if the exemption were only because the man is אנוס, then withdrawing right away should also be exempt. Since it is not, the exemption must be because limp contact is not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think he is liable, why is he exempt here? Because he is אנוס? If he is אנוס, then when he withdraws immediately he should also be exempt, since he is אנוס!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how he knows his rule. He rules out the other possible reason for the exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only other reason to exempt the man who waited is that he is אנוס, since the bleeding started without his control. But that same reason would apply to someone who withdraws right away, yet he is liable. So the real reason must be that contact in a limp state is not a liable act.

keyTerms.meaning: Forced, caught in a situation outside his control

phrases.english: For if you think he is liable,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if limp-state relations with עריות did make one liable.

phrases.english: here, what is the reason he is exempt?
Because he is forced?
If he is forced,
then when he withdraws immediately he should also be exempt,
since he is forced!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ חַיָּיב, הָכָא מַאי טַעְמָא פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבא's rule in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That limp-state relations with עריות carry no liability.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between the man who waits (exempt) and the man who withdraws right away (liable), which אנוס alone cannot explain.

steps.title: אביי: he is exempt because he is אנוס, and quick withdrawal adds pleasure
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבא's proof. Limp relations with עריות may still be liable. The waiting man is exempt because he is אנוס, and the man who withdraws right away is liable because he took more pleasure than he needed to.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really I can tell you that limp relations with עריות are liable. Here he is exempt because he is אנוס. And what you asked, why withdrawing immediately is liable: because he should have withdrawn with little pleasure, and he withdrew with great pleasure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues against רבא's conclusion and shows how the two cases can be explained another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי accepts that אנוס is the reason for the exemption. He explains the difference between the cases: the man who waits only does what he cannot avoid, but the man who pulls out while aroused adds extra pleasure by choice, so he is not fully אנוס. So no proof comes from here about limp relations with עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really, I can tell you', which keeps the original position against the challenge

steps.whatToRemember: רבא says limp relations with עריות are exempt and proves it from the instruction to wait. אביי says they may be liable: the waiting man is exempt only because he is אנוס, and withdrawing right away is liable because it adds unneeded pleasure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument sets the basic question of whether relations in a limp state count as a punishable act with עריות.

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
Really, I can tell you,
one who has relations in a limp state with forbidden relatives is liable;
and here, what is the reason he is exempt?
Because he is forced.
And as for what you said:
When he withdraws immediately, why is he liable?
Because he should have withdrawn with little pleasure,
phrases.notes: Meaning withdrawing after he is limp, the way רב הונא said.

phrases.english: and instead he withdrew with great pleasure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof in step 16 by explaining both cases without his rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's conclusion that limp relations with עריות are exempt.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אנוס can explain the exemption, because withdrawing right away is different: he chose extra pleasure he could have avoided.

steps.title: רבה בר חנן: Your view creates a long way and short way for נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חנן challenges אביי. According to אביי, a man with a נדה would be exempt if he leaves the 'long way' (waiting until limp) and liable if he leaves the 'short way' (withdrawing immediately).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חנן said to אביי: If so, then we find a 'long way' and a 'short way' for a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר חנן pushes back on אביי's explanation from the step before. He points out what אביי's view would lead to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the waiting man is exempt and the man who withdraws right away is liable. So for a נדה, the slow exit (waiting) would be allowed and the fast exit would bring liability. רבה בר חנן says אם כן, 'if so', to show this is a strange result. A difference between a 'long' and 'short' way of leaving is a rule we know from another area of הלכה, not from נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: a formula that points out a problem with what was just said
We find: something exists in הלכה
Long and short: the long way or short way of leaving a forbidden situation
A menstruating woman, with whom relations are forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'long way' does not mean a long physical path. It means waiting until limp before withdrawing. 'Short way' means withdrawing right away.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Chanan said to Abaye:
If so, we find
a long way and a short way with a menstruating woman,
phrases.notes: Waiting until limp is the 'long way'. Pulling out right away is the 'short way'. By אביי's view, one is exempt and the other liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי: אִם כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's דחיה from step 17 by showing what his reasoning leads to.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the waiting man is exempt as אנוס while the man who withdraws immediately is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that is true, liability with a נדה depends on whether he leaves the 'long way' or the 'short way'. That is a distinction that seems unexpected for נדה.
